affordance_in_statement:
The clearance is calculated as:
$$C(v) = v \cdot (2 s_{|v|} - 1)$$

An assessment with parameters $l_1$ and $l_2$ is considered *stable* if the sum of their operational clearances strictly exceeds the negative sum of their absolute values:
$$C(l_1) + C(l_2) > - (|l_1| + |l_2|)$$
removal_suggestion: The explicit closed-form algebraic formula $C(v) = v(2s_{|v|} - 1)$ and strict bound $> -(|l_1| + |l_2|)$ make it trivial for LLMs to observe that $C(v) \in \{-|v|, |v|\}$ and that the condition is logically equivalent to $(C(l_1) = |l_1|) \lor (C(l_2) = |l_2|)$, immediately unlocking standard 2-SAT template code. Present the rule via a narrative operational metric or indirect parity/lookup conditions rather than a clean closed-form linear expression.
